unnecessary line in the file ergm.pl that causes your error, and  
removing this line makes your code run.

You can source (or copy-and-paste) the attached file *after* loading  
ergm to remove the unnecessary line.

Naturally, this will be fixed in the next version of ergm, which  
should actually appear within this month.

Dave

terms of more intuitive analogs for a paper that I'm writing utilizing
ERGMs. 

I tend to think of GWESP and GWDSP as measures of local
clustering/efficiency 

in the network. Is it fair to think of GWNSP as a measure of global
efficiency

 (somewhat of a minimum geodesic distance analog) or am I completely off
base? 



Thanks, 

Sean

messages.body_plain:
Hi, Sean,

In short, GWNSP = GWDSP - GWESP  (with all coefficients and parameters
the same). I tend to view GWNSP as a measure of tension from having a
pair of actors linked by two-path(s) not having a tie between them, so I
wouldn't say that it's any more "global" than GWDSP.

                         I hope this helps,
                         Pavel Krivitsky

messages.subject_clean: [statnet_help] resolved: trouble 'finding' statnet on linux system
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

Thanks to advice from Mark Handcock, two things were giving me trouble 
and are now adequately resolved:

1) I was running a very old version of R: 2.7.2 on Ubuntu 8.04.  It was 
slightly challenging to get ubuntu to load the latest R binary.  It 
required adding a line like this:

   deb http://<my.favorite.cran.mirror>/bin/linux/ubuntu <http://%3Cmy.favorite.cran.mirror%3E/bin/linux/ubuntu> hardy/

in my /etc/apt/sources.list file.  Getting that to work should have been 
easier than it was, but that was simply a matter of getting correct syntax.

2) Even with the latest R, I still had a problem: in a nutshell, rgl, 
shapes and then latentnet did not load.  This turns out to be most 
likely a 64-bit R problem.  So for now, the solution will be either to 
use ergm, which has most of the same functionality as statnet, or load 
32-bit R.

Marc Scott

messages.subject: [statnet_help] Simulate and Estimate ERGM(THETA0)?
messages.body_plain:
Hi--

I've been trying to simulate and then estimate ERGM with various THETA values, but have had a really tough time getting the ERGM to estimate properly. I have also been sampling subgraphs to test out the performance of ERGM under Handcock and Giles missing edges framework. 

I have included the style of code that I have been trying which follows the following simple algorithm:
1. Initialize THETA0.
2. Sample A_N from ERGM(THETA0).
3. Estimate ERGM(THETA | A_N).
4. Sample a subgraph, A_M, of A_N.
5. Estimate ERGM(THETA | A_M+'NA's for unsampled edges). (Graph is still size N.)

I keep having issues with either Step #3 or Step #5 (or perhaps Step #2, since it is hard to validate whether ERGM(THETA0) is actually working well) when I estimate anything more exotic than A_N ~ edges. In particular, I would like to estimate almost anything other than this model, perhaps A_N ~ edges + triangles + kstars(3). However, these statistics are highly collinear (as in Snijder's work), so that may be part of the problem.

I really just want to simulate and estimate ANY ERGM(THETA0) model to see if I can get the parameters back.

I have taken a look at mcmc.diagnostics(), but perhaps don't fully understand how to use it, as even when it says that things have converged, I still have issues.

Any advice on how to get things to estimate properly? Do I need really, really large burn-ins and MCMCsamplesizes with large sampling intervals? Or can those exacerbate my estimation problems?

Thanks!

--Randall

P.S. See the code below that I have been testing using StatNet on R v2.8.1 (I've had a hard time downloading StatNet for the most recent versions of R. Is there a particular "best" server to get the full package from?). Thanks!
P.P.S. Is there a way to see the StatNet help archives without a UW account?

rm(list=ls())

library("ergm")

# "Get" the "W"orking "D"irectory.
getwd()
# "Set" the "W"orking "D"irectory.
setwd('C:\\Documents\ and\ Settings\\ralewis\\My\ Documents\\Arun-Spectrum-Indo')
# dir.create("ERGMsim")


N <- 30
psi <- .7 # Fraction of Network's Nodes that were sampled.
M <- ceiling(psi*N) # Number of sampled nodes.


theta <- c( 1.0*2*(runif(1)-.5), .05*2*(runif(1)*-.5), .05*2*(runif(1)-.5) )


# Generate a Network from ERGM(theta) of size N.
#A_N <- simulate(network(N,directed=FALSE) ~ edges                       , theta0 = theta[1], burnin = 250000, maxit = 5)
#A_N <- simulate(network(N,directed=FALSE) ~ edges + cycle(3)           , theta0 = theta[1:2], basis = A_N, burnin = 250000, maxit = 5)
#A_N <- simulate(network(N,directed=FALSE) ~ edges + cycle(3) + kstar(2), theta0 = theta, basis = A_N, burnin = 250000, maxit = 5)
A_N <- simulate(network(N,directed=FALSE) ~ edges + degree( , theta0 = theta[1:2], burnin = 250000, MCMCsamplesize=100000, maxit = 5)

# Estimate the First ERGM
# TrueFit <- ergm(A_N ~ edges )
# summary(TrueFit)
#TrueFit2 <- ergm(A_N ~ edges                       , burnin = 250000, maxit = 5)
#TrueFit2 <- ergm(A_N ~ edges + cycle(3)           , burnin = 250000, theta0 = c(TrueFit2$MCMCtheta[1],.01), maxit = 5)
TrueFit2 <- ergm(A_N ~ edges + cycle(3) , burnin = 250000, MCMCsamplesize=100000, interval=200, theta0 = theta[1:2]+c(-.2,.1), maxit = 5)
summary(TrueFit2)
mcmc.diagnostics(TrueFit2)

# Initialize the sampled network.
A_Nmissingmat <- A_N[,]

# Randomly Order the Nodes.
Sampled <- (order(runif(N))<=M)
# AllSampled[g,] <- Sampled

# Then replace the selected missing ones with 'NA'.
A_Nmissingmat[,!Sampled] <- NA
A_Nmissingmat[!Sampled,] <- NA
A_Nmissing <- network(A_Nmissingmat, directed=FALSE)

# Fit the ERGM with the Observed data.
# MissingFit <- ergm(A_Nmissing ~ edges , burnin = 250000, maxit = 5)
# summary(MissingFit)

MissingFit2 <- ergm(A_Nmissing ~ edges + cycle(3) , burnin = 250000, MCMCsamplesize=100000, interval=200, maxit = 10)#, theta0 = MissingFit2$MCMCtheta)
summary(MissingFit2)

messages.subject: [statnet_help] ERGM with Loops
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I am working with a network that has loops (self-ties) and was wondering if there is a way to add a statistic to the ERGM estimation that counts the number of loops?

I tried setting the vertex names as a vertex attribute and then ran nodematch using the names as the attribute.  This returned a 0 statistic, so it seems like it didn't consider the edges that are loops.

How does ERGM estimate with loops?  Does it consider the attributes just as it would another edge, or are the edges simply ignored?  Thanks for your help!

Sincerely,

Jared Stanfield
University of Washington

messages.subject: [statnet_help] ERGM with Loops
messages.body_plain:
Hi Jared,

Ergm was not written to handle loops, so it ignores that information.  If you want to consider the presence of a loop on a node as a fixed attribute and a predictor of other ties, you could code it as a binary nodal attribute.  But unfortunately there's no way to have nodal loops be an outcome of the stochastic process of tie formation in ergm.

Steve

messages.subject: [statnet_help] GWESP - parameter setting
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I am conducting my first analysis with statnet. More precisely, I am 
modeling information exchange between organizations in a directed 
network. For this purpose, I am including some edge covariates like 
preference similarity or common membership in policy committees, and 
some node factors like organizational type.

I would also like to capture the effect of transitivity: I have found 
strong theoretical hints that an actor is more likely to send 
information to another actor if the sender has an outgoing tie to a 
third party which in turn has an outgoing tie to the receiver. My hunch 
is that GWESP should be the 'weapon of choice'.

However, I do not fully understand what is captured by the scaling 
parameter alpha (or lambda?). If I do not fix this parameter (i.e. the 
default setting), the model fit as indicated by AIC and BIC is quite 
good, but the graphical goodness of fit assessment does *not* look very 
nice. If I fix the parameter at 0 or 0.1, the gof is really good, but 
AIC and BIC are much larger. If I increase the parameter value, AIC and 
BIC are decreased, but the graphical gof gets worse. How can I interpret 
the parameter and the 'fixed' option?

Many thanks!

Philip
